# Requirements + UX Checklist: Portfolio Baseline Definition

**Purpose**: Validate the quality, clarity, and coverage of the baseline portfolio
requirements with emphasis on public UX expectations and requirement writing strength.
**Created**: 2026-05-14
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the required homepage sections fully enumerated rather than implied through broad wording alone? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the spec explicitly define which public follow-up resources are in scope beyond generic examples such as email, repository, CV, or profile links? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the supported-language requirements complete enough to distinguish content parity from literal translation parity? [Completeness, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec define whether theme switching is part of the baseline experience or intentionally outside scope? [Gap]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is “core skill focus” specific enough to be evaluated objectively during review? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK006 Is “structured sections” clarified with minimum section expectations instead of relying only on narrative interpretation? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK007 Is “direct page navigation” specific enough to distinguish in-page anchors, top navigation, and other navigation affordances? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK008 Is “equivalent meaning and coverage” defined with enough precision to judge bilingual regressions consistently? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK009 Do the scope-boundary requirements align with the maintainer-facing acceptance scenario about explicit scope expansion? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK010 Are the non-goals in the specification consistent with the baseline constraints summarized in the implementation plan? [Consistency, Spec §FR-004, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK011 Do the user-story expectations for project review and contact follow-up align with the public experience contract without introducing stricter or looser rules? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 2]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK012 Can “identify the portfolio owner's profile, professional focus, and value proposition within 60 seconds” be assessed with a repeatable review method? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK013 Is “100% of featured work items and public contact actions lead to an intended destination” measurable when a destination is intentionally unavailable? [Clarity, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK014 Does the success criteria set define how to evaluate “content or presentation changes” versus “service-based application” changes objectively? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 Are requirements defined for both first-time visitors and maintainers with enough separation to avoid mixing audience expectations? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 1, Spec §User Story 3]
- [ ] CHK016 Are alternate content-consumption flows covered for visitors who only review projects or only review contact information? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK017 Are mobile and keyboard-only review scenarios covered by explicit requirements rather than only by edge-case notes? [Coverage, Edge Case]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK018 Does the spec define expected fallback behavior when a project link or public contact destination is unavailable? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the spec clarify what “little or no content” means for a section and what minimum UX outcome must still hold? [Clarity, Edge Case]
- [ ] CHK020 Are partial localization drift scenarios covered with a required maintainer response or acceptance boundary? [Coverage, Edge Case]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK021 Are accessibility expectations measurable enough to support review of keyboard reachability and readable content hierarchy? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK022 Are performance expectations quantified enough to interpret “fast first-pass reading experience” consistently across reviewers? [Clarity, Plan §Performance Goals]
- [ ] CHK023 Does the baseline define minimum UX expectations for responsive behavior across mobile and desktop beyond broad platform statements? [Completeness, Plan §Target Platform]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK024 Are assumptions about public external links documented in a way that prevents hidden dependency on third-party services for core browsing? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK025 Is the assumption that future service-backed features will be separately specified supported by an explicit governance trigger, not just implied intent? [Consistency, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK026 Are dependencies on bilingual content maintenance documented strongly enough to flag ownership when one locale lags behind? [Gap]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK027 Is there any conflict between describing the site as “static-first” and allowing external resource destinations that may depend on outside availability? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK028 Does the spec distinguish clearly between required third-party integrations and optional outbound links to third-party destinations? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK029 Are “public professional presentation experience” and “service-based application” defined clearly enough to avoid subjective review disputes? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions, Spec §SC-004]

## Notes

- Intended audience: author
- Depth: standard
- Focus areas: requirements-quality, ux-requirements
- This checklist tests the written requirements and UX requirement coverage, not whether the implementation works.
